steps.title: Continuity
steps.body: For $x\ne 0$, $|x|$ equals $x$ or $-x$, both continuous. At $0$: $\lim_{x\to0^-}(-x)=0=\lim_{x\to0^+}x=f(0)$. So $f$ is continuous everywhere — **P is true**.

steps.title: Differentiability at 0
steps.body:
Left derivative: $\lim_{h\to0^-}\frac{|h|-0}{h}=\frac{-h}{h}=-1$.

Right derivative: $\lim_{h\to0^+}\frac{|h|}{h}=1$.

$-1\ne 1$, so $f'(0)$ does not exist — **Q is false**.

P is true: $|x|$ is continuous at every point.

P is true, so 'both false' is wrong.

pitfalls: Differentiability implies continuity, but not the other way round — $|x|$ is the standard counterexample.
